teaser: The PHP story's work and who did it, nine names with their responsibilities, and its evidence vault opened to everyone, scanned before the key was published.
core_idea: A story with many agent writers needs its work, its roles and its evidence written down where anyone can check them: a work file the build holds to its rules, roles drawn from the record, and an evidence vault opened with a read key only after a scan, read in the browser one source at a time.

nodes.label: Nine names, one chat
nodes.summary: The editor, three long-lived agents, an app builder and four collectors worked the story in a day.

nodes.label: The work as a file
nodes.summary: work.json: 24 rows, each with an owner, a status, times and proof.

nodes.label: Two rules the build keeps
nodes.summary: An owner must be a known name, and a finished row must name its proof.

nodes.label: Roles from the record
nodes.summary: What each name may and must not change, drawn from git logs and vault commits.

nodes.label: A name kept, not rewritten
nodes.summary: The morning name stays in the history, with the reason, so the record can be checked.

nodes.label: The vault opened read-only
nodes.summary: A public read key that reads every file and cannot write.

nodes.label: The scan before the key
nodes.summary: 1,839 files searched for keys, tokens and personal data; none found, three things noted.

nodes.label: Public for good
nodes.summary: A published read key cannot be withdrawn from anyone who has fetched the objects.

nodes.label: The browser that could not open it
nodes.summary: After four minutes and 742 requests the vault browser was still reading.

nodes.label: Read one source at a time
nodes.summary: The manifest in about three seconds, a source in about seven, screenshots on request.

nodes.label: A review for the story's site
nodes.summary: Ten changes ranked by impact, each against an article here, sent as a zip.

nodes.label: The move's five checks
nodes.summary: Read from the same file as the section, so the two cannot disagree.

quotes.text: A history that changes its names when someone is renamed is a history nobody can check.
quotes.why: Why the roles keep a retired name instead of rewriting the record.

quotes.text: A published read key cannot be withdrawn from anyone who has fetched the objects, so before publishing it I scanned the whole vault, captures included
quotes.why: The order that matters when opening a vault.
